name: dzùùngoo de Samogohiri

catalog_quote: Comme la plupart des langues de la famille Niger Congo, le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale. Nous adopterons ici la définition d'une langue tonale qu'en donne Denis Creissels: "toute langue où une commutation phonologiquement limitée à la hauteur ou à la mélodie d'une syllabe unique est susceptible de constituer la seule trace d'une commutation entre deux unités significatives minimales dans une construction inchangée" (Creissels, 94, 175). [...] Le système tonal du dzùùngoo présente trois niveaux de hauteur tonale lexicalement significatifs que nous désignerons comme ton haut (H), ton moyen (M) et ton bas (B).
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Comme la plupart des langues de la famille Niger Congo, le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale. Nous adopterons ici la définition d'une langue tonale qu'en donne Denis Creissels : "toute langue où une commutation phonologiquement limitée à la hauteur ou à la mélodie d'une syllabe unique est susceptible de constituer la seule trace d'une commutation entre deux unités significatives minimales dans une construction inchangée" (Creissels, 94, 175). [...] Le système tonal du dzùùngoo présente trois niveaux de hauteur tonale lexicalement significatifs que nous désignerons comme ton haut (H), ton moyen (M) et ton bas (B).
new_statements.translation: Like most languages of the Niger-Congo family, Dzùùngoo is a tone language. We adopt here Denis Creissels' definition of a tone language: 'any language in which a commutation phonologically limited to the pitch or melody of a single syllable can constitute the only trace of a commutation between two minimal meaningful units in an otherwise unchanged construction' (Creissels 1994: 175). [...] The tone system of Dzùùngoo presents three lexically significant levels of pitch, which we will call high tone (H), mid tone (M) and low tone (B).
new_statements.citation: Solomiac, Paul. 2007. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du Dzùùngoo de Samogohiri. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (dir. Denis Creissels), NNT 2007LYO20060. Chapter 6 'Le système tonal'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (55 pp., PrimoPDF from "Thèse.doc", author SOLOMIAC). extracted text of PDF page 1 (printed p. 147; "148" appears at the foot of page 2) gives exactly: "6 LE SYSTÈME tonal / Comme la plupart des langues de la famille Niger Congo, le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale. Nous adopterons ici la définition d'une langue tonale qu'en donne Denis Creissels : "toute langue où une commutation phonologiquement limitée à la hauteur ou à la mélodie d'une syllabe unique est susceptible de constituer la seule trace d'une commutation entre deux unités significatives minimales dans une construction inchangée" (Creissels, 94, 175). / 6.1 INTRODUCTION / Le système tonal du dzùùngoo présente trois niveaux d…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Dzùùngoo is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L; TBU = mora; floating H; automatic downstep after L). The description contains no statement about word stress at all — neither a placement rule nor an explicit denial; the chapter on 'le mot phonologique' (ch. 5, not archived) is summarised by the reviewer as covering syllable combinations, reduplication, word length and vowel harmony only.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. One incidental use of 'accent'/'syllabe accentuée' on p. 89 (ch. 3) concerns the H-toned diminutive suffix -rɪ́ in a historical comparison with Jula diminutives, not a stress rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on nouns and verbs (citation forms and in the utterance); tone assignment discussed at word and phrase level; no stress domain stated.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes the Dzùùngoo of Samogohiri (Burkina Faso, near the Malian border), the main variety of ISO dnn / Glottolog dzuu1241 (Solomiac calls it 'dzùùngoo, appelé aussi samogho'). Not to be confused with Duungooma (duun1242, Mali) or the other Samogo languages (Bankagooma, Jowulu, Seenku, Kpeengo).

tone_statements.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2018. A survey of word-level replacive tonal patterns in Western Mande. Mandenkan 59: 67-108. DOI 10.4000/mandenkan.1420.
tone_statements.quote: In chapter 6 the author presents the tonal system of the language, using Keith Snider’s Register Tier Theory (RTT). This theory makes use of a register tier, a pitch tier and a tonal node tire in order to account for such phenomena as downstep and a floating high tone. Three tones are identified as tonemes: High, Mid and Low, and contrary to the usual rule postulated in autosegmental theories, the author posits a right to left assignment of tones to tone bearing units (moras), adding some rules.
tone_statements.locator: paragraph <6> of the HTML version (unpaginated online review; archived HTML galley of AAeO 2015/4269)

tone_statements.citation: Solomiac, Paul. 2017. Le conditionnel en Dzuungoo de Somogohiri. Studies in African Linguistics 46(1). DOI 10.32473/sal.v46i1.107244.
tone_statements.quote: In the Samogho group, word-level RT phenomena have been reported for Dzùùngo in Solomiac (2007:365–380) which appear to be more in keeping with what is observed in Central Mande languages. The examples in (31), adapted from Solomiac’s thesis, illustrate various tonal outcomes in Dzùùngo compounds. When W1 begins with a lexical /L/ tone, regardless of the lexical tonal melody of W2, one of two possibilities is observed. Either the surface tonal melody of the compound is [L#H] (31a) or it is [L#M(H)], where a tone in parentheses indicates a floating tone (31b). When W1 begins with either a lexical /H/ or /M/ tone, two additional outcomes are possible. Either the surface tonal melody of the resulting compound is [M#H], as in (31c), or it is [M#M(H)], as in (31d).
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 (H, M, L) plus floating H, as presupposed in the compound melodies

tone_statements.citation: Dombrowsky-Hahn, Klaudia. 2015. Paul Solomiac: Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du dzùùngoo [review of Solomiac 2014, Mande Languages and Linguistics 10, Köln: Köppe]. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online (AAeO) 2015, Book reviews. DOI 10.18716/ojs/aaeo/2015_3416; URN urn:nbn:de:0009-10-42696.
tone_statements.quote: Le dzùùngoo est une langue tonale à trois tons, haut (H), transcrit avec un accent aigu sur la voyelle, moyen (M), pas transcrit, et bas (B), transcrit avec un accent grave sur la voyelle. Les deux morphèmes du conditionnel sont à ton M.
tone_statements.translation: Dzùùngoo is a tone language with three tones, high (H), transcribed with an acute accent on the vowel, mid (M), not transcribed, and low (B), transcribed with a grave accent on the vowel. The two conditional morphemes bear M tone.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones, high, mid and low (high and low written with acute and grave accents, mid unmarked); stated in passing, no further tonal analysis in this article.

Nothing on word stress / accent d'intensité / prominence in the 55 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent, accentu, intensité, proéminence, stress, prosod, suprasegment; only hits are 'tendance.. accentuée' = marked tendency, p. 187).
Abstract: phoneme inventory (ch. 3), syllabic structure of the word (chs. 2, 4, 5), tonal structure (ch. 6); 'accessible: oui' but no URL; Lyon 2 server refused connections.

tone.says: Word-level replacive tone ('compacité tonale') in Dzùùngoo compounds, after Solomiac 2007: 365-380: the compound melody is determined by the initial lexical tone of W1 - W1 with initial /L/ gives [L#H] or [L#M(H)] (floating H in parentheses), W1 with initial /H/ or /M/ gives [M#H] or [M#M(H)]; which of the two variants surfaces is not predictable from W1 and seems conditioned by W2 in a still unclear way; examples fòròbà#níí 'communal cow', fààmà#dzīnˊ 'prince', nānmārā#móó 'spy', dūūn#gōōˊ 'th…
